title: The pullback of module objects preserves K-flat quasi-isomorphisms
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and $f\colon X\to Y$ a morphism of
schemes. The pullback $f^*\colon\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ of module objects
([sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]), applied termwise, sends quasi-isomorphisms
between K-flat complexes of $\Lambda_Y$-modules to quasi-isomorphisms
([sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]).

proof.text: For $Z=X,Y$, use the small pro-étale sites of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] with $\mathcal A=\Ab$, $\Sh(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ is abelian symmetric monoidal with additive tensor, and tensoring preserves all colimits. In particular $\Lambda_Z\otimes-$ preserves finite colimits, so [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] applied to the coefficient ring object $\Lambda_Z$ makes $\Mod_{\Lambda_Z}$ abelian.

source.place: Entire abelianness criterion, applied to the sheaf categories supplied by lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed; compare Stacks sites-modules.tex Tags 03DA (lemma-abelian), 03EI (lemma-sheafification-exact), 03EO (lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor).

proof.text: Apply [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main] to the given commutative condensed ring $\Lambda$ and arbitrary scheme morphism $f$. It states that the very composite $f^*=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\Ab})$ of the item is additive and preserves finite limits and finite colimits. Thus it is an exact functor between the abelian categories of step 1.

source.place: Entire proposition, first assertion; supplies the exactness invoked in the opening sentence of the item proof.

proof.text: Let $s:P\to P'$ be a quasi-isomorphism and fix $n\in\mathbf Z$. Regard its three components in degrees $n-1,n,n+1$ as a morphism $a:S\to T$ of short complexes. In the abelian categories of step 1, step 2 ensures that $f^*$ preserves the two cycle kernels and the cokernels of the two maps into cycles. Apply [lem-sfb-local-homology-quasi-iso] to these diagrams. It supplies $c_V:H(f^*V)\xrightarrow{\sim}f^*H(V)$ and the naturality identity $H(f^*a)=c_T^{-1}\circ f^*(H(a))\circ c_S$. Since $H(a)=H^n(s)$ is invertible, its final assertion gives invertibility of $H^n(f^*s)$.

source.place: Second clause: an exact functor applied termwise commutes with cohomology; the cited node supplies the natural comparison, based on Stacks Tags 010N and 015F.

proof.text: The preceding argument holds for every integer $n$. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $f^*s$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This applies in particular when $P,P'$ are K-flat, giving the asserted restriction.

source.place: Final clause: sends every quasi-isomorphism, hence every quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes, to a quasi-isomorphism.
